name: Bagdad
lede: Bagdad is a very dark blue from Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary, using the older English spelling of the Iraqi city; why the city lent its name is undocumented.

sections.title: A dictionary name and an old spelling
sections.body: Maerz and Paul's dictionary lists Bagdad at plate 40, position L 7, and the library dates its first recorded use to 1921; the NBS cited it in 1955 [1]. The nearest ISCC-NBS category is plain dark blue, about 4.7 units away [1]. Nothing in our books explains the name. Birren, discussing early color symbolism, cites Woolley on a ziggurat found between Bagdad and the Persian Gulf, dated to about 2300 BC, whose shrine was covered in blue glazed tile; that is the only link the books offer [2]. Neighbors are [[trooper]], [[dark-grey-blue]] and [[prussian-blue]] [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Bagdad appears in 265 of the 23,781 paintings in our archive (1.1%), as photographed [4]. Its most devoted painter is Émile Bernard, who uses it in 4 of 22 works here, 6.1 times the baseline of the museums those works come from [4]. Like Atlantis it is mostly a hidden color: in 47% of the 139 paintings where it counts [4]. These are photographs of varnished paintings, not pigment tests.
